steps: Shape your dominant hand into a flattened O, thumb pad pressed under the fingertips.
Hold your non-dominant hand low in front of you, fingers together and palm cupped upward as the base.
Move the dominant hand down and settle it into the base hand, as if placing an object where it belongs.
Keep the dominant fingertips pointing down as they land, with the base palm staying open and level.
Keep your face and shoulders neutral; this is a plain placing gesture, not an emphatic one.
tip: INSTALL is the 'put there' version of PUT — for software, keep the motion small and quick.

steps: Pinch the thumb against the index finger on each hand, forming two small pincers.
Grip your shirt fabric on each side of your upper chest, pinching between thumb and index finger.
Tug the fabric outward away from your body two or three times in short, even pulls.
Keep your palms angled down and slightly inward while you pinch and tug.
Use a neutral, describing expression — you are naming the garment, not offering to help.
tip: Use two hands for SHIRT — the one-handed version is how signers say VOLUNTEER.

steps: Shape your dominant hand into an F, thumb touching the index fingertip to close the circle.
Hold your non-dominant hand flat in front of you at chest height, palm facing straight up.
Touch the pinched tip of the F hand to the base palm near its heel, then slide it forward twice.
Keep the base palm level and facing up; turn the F hand's palm sideways during the slides.
Count with a focused, neutral face — this is a tallying motion, not a question.
tip: Add the 'person' ending to COUNT and you get ACCOUNTANT — literally 'counting person.'

steps: Bring up your dominant hand with the fingers held together and straight.
Start with the fingertips touching the center of your left breast.
Lift slightly and bring the fingertips down onto the center of your right breast in an even second touch.
Keep your palm turned toward your body so the fingertips land flat on the chest.
Keep your face matter-of-fact — BREAST is an anatomical term, not an emotional one.
tip: Two touches, left then right — the doubled movement is what makes it BREAST; it is also the base of the BREASTFEED compound.
